79K likes, 473 comments - plantbasedrd on September 4, 2026: "my current favorite way to use up all that zucchini, zucchini pancakes ✨ btw also freezes well if you want to make a bunch at once

2 medium zucchini, ~450g
1, 16 oz container silken tofu, 454g
1 tsp kosher salt (plus more as needed)
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, spoon and leveled, 188g
1/2 cup potato starch (or 6 tbsp cornstarch), spoon and leveled, 85g
1 tsp baking powder
1/4 cup sesame seeds plus more for sprinkling on top
1 small red onion, thinly sliced
4 scallions, thinly sliced
3 cloves garlic, grated
1 inch ginger, grated
Avocado oil for cooking

✅ Detailed blog post linked in profile 

If using zucchini, thinly slice or shred it using a box grater or shredding tool. Transfer to a large mixing bowl, sprinkle with a generous pinch of salt, then toss to coat. Allow the zucchini to sit for 5 mins to help draw out some moisture. Gather the zucchini in your hands above the bowl (or sink) and squeeze out as much liquid as possible. Pat the shreds dry with a paper towel, then clear out your mixing bowl.

To a blender cup add the silken tofu and salt. Blend until completely smooth.

To the same large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, potato starch, and baking powder. Pour in the tofu mixture and whisk until you form a very thick batter. 

Break apart the shredded zucchini into the batter along with the onions, scallions, garlic, ginger, and sesame seeds. Use a spatula to evenly fold the vegetables into the batter.

Place an 8-inch pan over medium-low heat, then add about 1 tbsp of oil to coat the bottom (alternatively, use a large griddle to cook all the pancakes at once). Dollop a third of the batter into the pan, then spread the mixture out evenly with a spatula. Cook undisturbed for 7 mins, or until the bottom is golden. Sprinkle the uncooked side of the pancake with some sesame seeds and a drizzle of oil, then flip and cook for 6-7 mins, or until equally golden in color. Transfer the pancake to a wire rack, clear out the pan, add additional oil and cook the remaining batter. You should end up with about 3 large pancakes.

To serve, cut up your pancake as desired. Serve with your favorite dip and enjoy immediately! #plantbasedrecipes #zucchini".

audio.transcript: If you happen to have a lot of zucchini on hand and need a way to get through them quick, maybe just turn them into some savory pancakes. I recently made a stack of these to store in the freezer and they are convenient to reheat and a fun way to get in some extra veggies. Now, these pancakes are thick with crispy edges and to get that perfect texture, we need to remove as much moisture from our zucchini as possible. Drain it well, then prep the batter, which is a combo of some flour and blended silken tofu. This combo gives you a thick batter that is essential for getting a satisfying, bouncy texture without having to use any eggs. From here, it's just combining everything in one bowl, all that shredded zucchini, lots of onions, garlic and ginger. Once everything is evenly mixed, scoop a heaping portion of that batter into a greased pan and cook it until both sides are nice and golden.
